subject: physics
title: Visible light and colour
key_idea: (Separate science) Each colour of visible light has its own wavelength and frequency. An object's colour depends on which wavelengths it reflects, absorbs or transmits. A filter transmits some wavelengths and absorbs the rest.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers what colour means for light.

items: Each colour of visible light has its own narrow band of wavelength and frequency.
The colours run from red (longest wavelength) to violet (shortest wavelength).
White light is a mixture of all the colours.
Our eyes can only detect a limited range of the electromagnetic spectrum.
Other animals detect different ranges. A bee detects ultraviolet but cannot detect red.
(Separate science) Each colour has its own band of wavelength and frequency.
Red has the longest wavelength and violet the shortest.
Our eyes detect only visible light.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers what happens to light when it meets an object.

items.meaning: Reflection from a smooth surface in a single direction.
Reflection from a rough surface, which scatters the light in many directions.
A material that transmits light so you can see clearly through it.
A material that transmits some light but through which you cannot see clearly.

items: The colour of an opaque object is decided by which wavelengths are more strongly reflected.
The wavelengths that are not reflected are absorbed.
A white object reflects all wavelengths equally.
A black object absorbs all wavelengths.
A red object reflects red light and absorbs the other colours.
(Separate science) An opaque object takes the colour of the wavelengths it reflects most.
Other wavelengths are absorbed.
White reflects all wavelengths equally. Black absorbs them all.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers colour filters and objects seen in coloured light. Pick a case to see the result.

items: A colour filter absorbs certain wavelengths and transmits others.
A green filter transmits green light and absorbs all the other colours.
An object in coloured light can only reflect the colours that are in that light.

diagram.alt: Pick an object or filter and a colour of light to see what colour you see.
diagram.prompt: Pick an object or filter and the light that shines on it

options.label: Red object in white light
results: All the other colours are absorbed.

options.label: White object in green light
results: All the green light is reflected.

options.label: White light through a green filter
results: All the other colours are absorbed.

options.label: Blue object seen through a green filter
results: The green filter only transmits green. The object reflects only blue, so no light is transmitted to the eye.
The blue light is absorbed by the filter.

options.label: Red light through a blue filter

blocks.text: To explain a colour, say what is reflected, transmitted or absorbed for each wavelength.

items: (Separate science) A filter transmits some wavelengths and absorbs the rest.
A coloured object looks black if the light shining on it has none of the wavelengths it reflects.
Always name the colour that is reflected, transmitted or absorbed.

checks.q: Describe what happens to white light shining on a blue filter.
checks.a: Only blue light is transmitted. All the other colours (wavelengths) are absorbed.

checks.q: A red flower is lit by green light. What colour does it appear? Explain.
checks.a: Black. The flower reflects only red light and absorbs the green light, so no light is reflected.

checks.q: What colour is an object that reflects all wavelengths equally?

worked_example.question:
Some reading glasses contain lenses made from blue glass. The blue glass acts as a filter.

Describe what happens to white light incident on colourless glass and white light incident on blue glass.
answer_points: Colourless glass: the white light is transmitted.
Blue glass: only blue light is transmitted.
All the other colours (wavelengths, frequencies) of light are absorbed.
worked_example.tip: Say what happens to each colour. A statement that blue glass absorbs green and red light is also accepted.

worked_example.question:
White light includes all the colours in the visible spectrum.

A beam of white light is the only light that shines on a book. The book appears green.

A red filter is placed between the source of white light and the book.

What colour does the book appear now?
answer_points: The red filter transmits only red light, so no green light shines on the book.
The book reflects only green light, so no light is reflected.
worked_example.tip: Only the colour black scores the mark. The reasons are not marked here but are what you would write if asked to explain.

worked_example.question:
This question is about visible light.

The fish appears red under white light.

Explain why the fish appears black under green light.
answer_points: The fish absorbs the green light (it does not reflect green light). It reflects red light only.
There is no red light in the green light to reflect, so no light is reflected.
worked_example.tip: One mark for what the fish does with the green light and one mark for why no red light is reflected.

worked_example.question:
A ray of light is monochromatic red light with a wavelength of 680 nm in air.

Define monochromatic.
worked_example.tip: Single colour is not enough on its own. Say that the light has one frequency.

blocks.text: The seven colours in order, from the longest wavelength and lowest frequency to the shortest wavelength and highest frequency, are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

items.meaning: (Supplement) Visible light of a single frequency, so a single colour.

blocks.text: The colours of the visible spectrum in order, from the longest wavelength and lowest frequency to the shortest wavelength and highest frequency:

items: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.
Red has the longest wavelength and the lowest frequency.
Violet has the shortest wavelength and the highest frequency.
